newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley probes offensive e-mail.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley probes offensive e-mail.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co., named in a racial discrimination lawsuit in December, said Friday it was investigating the source of offensive electronic mail that plaintiffs allege circulated through the printer's computer system.
R.R. Donnelly spokesman William Lowe said the company received documents listing 165 racial, ethnic and sexual jokes said to be created at a Donnelley plant in Lancaster, Pa.
"We haven't confirmed it, but it looks to be a Donnelley document," Lowe said. "The question is when, how, by whom and where was this created and how was it distributed."

In a statement, Jonathan Ward, R.R. Donnelley executive vice president and president of the company's commercial print unit, said, "We have zero tolerance for discrimination, and this act is a clear violation of our explicit company policy and values."

The $500 million class-action lawsuit charges that R.R. Donnelley discriminated against black employees when arranging transfers to other jobs in 1993 related to a plant closing. The company has denied the charges. No date has been set for a hearing.
Donnelley said its minority employment level totals about 13 percent. It said jobs held by blacks advanced 7 percent between 1995 and 1996.
